messages.subject: Error in Part 1,  'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double'
parts:
Hi GGRI Community and Dr. Van Hees, 

I am currently using GGRI to analyze data collected on Actigraph GT9X links. We are having trouble in step 1 with processing the csv file (we converted the raw GT3x file to a csv file using the ActiLife software). Upon running our script we received the error message: 

Error in (function (mode = 1:5, datadir = c(), outputdir = c(), studyname = c(),  : 

  'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double'

We are not sure if the problem lies in the csv file or the code itself. Would you be able to review both and let us know?

Here is R script we have been using: 

#=============================

# General parameters

#=============================

library (GGIR)

g.shell.GGIR(

  mode=1,

  dataadir= “/Volumes/GGIR Data/TEST",

  outputdir="/Volumes/GGIR Data/OUTPUT",

  studyname = "TEST",

  asDataFrame = TRUE,

  f0=1,

  f1=1,

  overwrite = FALSE,

  do.imp=TRUE,

  idloc=2,

  print.filename=TRUE,

  storefolderstructure=TRUE,

#=============================

# Part 1

#=============================

  windowsizes = c(1,900,3600),

  do.cal=TRUE,

  do.anglez=TRUE,

  do.enmo=TRUE,

  do.mad=FALSE,

  do.hfen=FALSE,

  do.en=FALSE,

  chunksize=1,

  printsummary=TRUE,

#=============================

# Part 2

#=============================

  strategy = 2,

  hrs.del.start = 0,

  hrs.del.end = 0,

  maxdur = 5,

  ndayswindow=7,

  includedaycrit = 10, 

  qwindo=c(0,24),

  mvpathreshold = c(50,200,700),

  mvpadur=c(1,5,10),

  boutcriter = c(0.8),

  bout.metric = 4,

  closedbout=FALSE,

  M5L5res = 10, 

  qM5L5 = c(0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9),

  winhr = c(1,6),

  ilevels = c(0,50,100,150,200,250,300,350,700,8000),

  excludefirstlast = TRUE,

  includenightcrit = 16,

  iglevels = TRUE,

  MX.ig.min.dur = 1,

  qlevels = c(960/1440,1320/1440,1380/1440,1410/1440,1425/1440,1435/1440),

#=============================

# Part 3+4 

#=============================

  timethreshold=5,

  anglethreshold=5,

  ignorenonwear = TRUE,

  def.noc.sleep = 1,

  outliers.only = FALSE,

  criterror = 4,

  do.visual = TRUE,

#=============================

# Part 5

#=============================

  iglevels = TRUE,

  winhr = c(1),

  M5L5res = c(60),

  threshold.lig = c(35.6),

  threshold.mod = c(201.4),

  threshold.vig = c(707.0),

  boutcriter = 0.8,

  boutcriter.in = 0.9,

  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,

  boutdur.in = c(1,10,30),

  boutdur.lig = c(1,10),

  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),

  timewindow = c("WW", "MM"),

  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

  frag.metrics="all",

  part5_agg2_60seconds=TRUE,

#=============================

# Visual Report

#=============================

  do.report=c(2),

  visualreport=FALSE,

  dofirstpage=TRUE,

  epochvalues2csv=TRUE,

  viewingwindow=1)

See csv file below:


We would really appreciate any help or advice on how we can resolve the error message. 


Thank you so much!

Best,
Aidan Loh

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Error in Part 1, 'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double'
parts:
Hi Aidan,

Someone may spot this quickly, but here's my take...

What version of GGIR are you using? g.shell.GGIR was deprecated so you can just change that to GGIR(....)
You also have a typo in part2 qwindo(missing w).
I also call mode as mode=c(1), though that probably won't help.

R is telling you what the problem is, it just doesn't say where inside the big GGIR shell function... I can't immediately detect see anything obvious other than the above. I suggest you deactivate lines related to modes 2:5 and try it, then add commands for mode 2,3,4,5 until the error pops up, that will help you pin down where abouts it is.

parts:
Hello, 

Thank you very much for your response and for helping me with our error. We discovered that winhr,iglevels, M5L5res,and  boutcriter were repeated twice throughout the R script. When we deleted the duplicate the R script ran smoothly. 

Thanks, 
Aidan

parts:
Hi.

What version of GGIR are you using, did you try the GitHub development version too?

You use a lot of input arguments, did you try processing the file with GGIR default values? 

asDataFrame is not a GGIR argument and should be removed.

Vincent
